profile.reading: AiNET's CyberNAP Glen Burnie facility occupies a converted three story former department store attached to a suburban mall at 7842 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie, Maryland 21061, roughly 10 miles north of Fort Meade. AiNET's own current CyberNAP page describes a 300,000 square foot facility on a 15 acre campus, with more than 80 megawatts of power capacity available from two separate electrical grids in a dual 2N redundant configuration, and power density exceeding 25 kilowatts per cabinet facility wide, positioning it as the largest standalone data center in the Maryland, Northern Virginia, and Washington DC region. A March 2012 Data Center Knowledge article on the building's conversion states each floor carries a 20 foot ceiling able to support heavy floor loads, capacity for up to 10,000 server cabinets, 1,500 parking spaces available for container deployment, and an opening planned for July 2012. The article identifies this as AiNET's third data center facility, and states the company, founded in 1993, targeted the site at enterprises and federal government agencies with a particular focus on Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility, or SCIF, requirements, given the proximity to Fort Meade's National Security Agency and Department of Defense operations. AiNET's own page describes three tiered security zones at the facility: a Commercial Security Zone with biometric access, an Advanced Security Zone exceeding NIST SP 800 requirements, and an Ultra Security Zone meeting NISPOM, DoD 8500, and ICD 705.2 and 705.3, or SCIF and DIACAP, standards. The facility functions as a carrier hotel with direct fiber interconnection to northeast corridor routes and access to AiNET's own DWDM fiber network. AiNET is headquartered at a separate Beltsville, Maryland facility already on file elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
CyberNAP Glen Burnie occupies 15 acres and roughly 300,000 square feet in a converted department store north of Fort Meade, Maryland, on Ritchie Highway. The operator has not published the facility's IT capacity in megawatts, so its power allocation to AI workloads cannot be assessed from public data.

Maryland has 11 mapped data center facilities, of which only 3 have published power figures totaling 9.3 megawatts. This campus ranks fourth among published capacities in the state, meaning at least one facility has disclosed more capacity than CyberNAP Glen Burnie, yet this campus still lacks a published figure, so that ranking reflects incomplete information.

Without published power consumption, the scale of this facility relative to AI infrastructure deployment cannot be determined. The building's origin as a converted retail structure and its suburban location near a federal facility constrain its relevance to the grid-as-binding-constraint question unless the operator discloses actual IT load.
